top_news.title: "Committed to support India's mission to eliminate Sickle cell disease": Habib Bennaceur, SVP Novo Nordisk
top_news.summary: Novo Nordisk, a Danish multinational pharmaceutical company, has expressed support for India's mission to eliminate sickle cell disease by 2047, highlighting the need for early diagnosis, public awareness, better healthcare infrastructure and improved access to treatment. Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a chronic single gene disorder causing a debilitating systemic syndrome characterized by chronic anemia, acute painful episodes, organ infarction and chronic organ damage and by a significant reduction in life expectancy. Habib Bennaceur, Senior Vice President of the Rare Disease Unit at Novo Nordisk, said India accounts for a significant share of the global sickle cell disease burden, with around 10 million people living with the condition worldwide. Explaining the impact of the disease, speaking to ANI, Bennaceur said it affects the shape of red blood cells and their ability to carry oxygen, potentially causing anaemia and serious complications. "Actually, sickle cell disease is an inherited disease that will affect the red blood cell shapes and will limit the transport of oxygen, which is the role of the red blood cell, to organs and to the organism, which will result in anaemia. It might also result as well in multiple organ damage, strokes, heart issues, kidney failures, and also sickle cell disease is also very well known for vaso-occlusive crises, deep severe pain that will force patients to go to hospital and be hospitalised for a long duration sometimes. So it's a very severe disease that has multiple complex complications in the organism," Bennaceur said. Explaining the company's interest in the disease, he said the unmet medical needs of patients and Novo Nordisk's experience in treating blood disorders, particularly haemophilia, prompted it to invest in sickle cell disease. "Novo is first guided by the unmet need and patient needs. So sickle cell disease has been left on the side of innovation for a very long time. It's a large population globally; there are 10 million people living with sickle cell disease over the world. And India is the second largest country in that aspect. And our long legacy in haemophilia, so with our portfolio there, it was a natural move to go and invest in making a difference in sickle cell disease with the ambition to defeat sickle cell disease," he said. Bennaceur added that the company was committed to supporting patients, medical professionals and the central and state governments in achieving the 2047 target. "India is the second-largest country in the world in terms of sickle cell disease prevalence, which means as a global pharma company, as Novo, we cannot decently say we are invested in sickle cell disease if we don't support and make a difference in India. But India is facing what many countries globally are facing in terms of the severity of the disease and the complications, but India is leading in many ways, actually and in the understanding of the fact that if you want to improve sickle cell disease, you need to work first on diagnosis. You need to work first on awareness, education, and infrastructure. And that's again one of the reasons of our visits here is one to learn about the critical sickle cell disease mission elimination for 2047, but also to commit to the Indian community to support all patients, the medical community and also the government, central and state government, in that mission," he said. He said the company was supporting projects focused on improving diagnosis and awareness, including the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) Hub and wellness hub. He cited the lack of diagnosis and treatment as a major challenge in parts of sub-Saharan Africa. "We already started the support by working on many projects, one of them being the SPOC Hub, but also the wellness hub, which is obviously first to improve the first medical contact, working on first diagnosis and awareness. There's a reason why, in sub-Saharan African countries, for example, 90% of kids born with sickle cell disease will die before the age of five is because they're not diagnosed and thus not even treated," he said. He added that Novo Nordisk was developing potential treatments, with its most advanced candidate having reached Phase 3 trials with positive results. The results were scheduled to be presented at the American Society of Rheumatology Congress in December. Vikrant Shrotriya, Corporate Vice President and Managing Director of Novo Nordisk India, said clinical trials had been completed and the company was working with regulatory authorities to make the treatment available in India as soon as possible. "The trials are finished. We are working very closely, obviously, with regulatory authorities and relevant authorities here to make it available as soon as possible," Shrotriya said. Shrotriya said India had an estimated 1.5 million to two million people living with sickle cell disease and that the company was conducting research on potential treatments in the country. "Coming to the blood disorder, we came with one of our products called Nova 7. Over a period of time, we have got many factors in this area of haemophilia. So it was very natural that we started working in the sickle cell area. So we have got a couple of molecules, and for those molecules we are so proud because India has got a dubious distinction of being second in the world with the highest population of sickle cell, 1.5 to 2 million people. Every sixth or seventh person in the world for sickle cell is actually in India," he added. Expressing hope that the forum would strengthen efforts towards the 2047 target, Shrotriya said,"So I am very, very happy that along with the Danish Embassy, Novo Nordisk, Niti Aayog, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, many of the stakeholders who are involved therein have come together to take a pledge that we would work together for sickle cell elimination, which was called by Prime Minister Modi by 2047. So, this is just the start of that advocacy of that movement, and I wish and hope that this becomes strengthened over a period of time." The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (NSCEM) was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 1, 2023, with the goal of eliminating Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) as a public health problem in India by 2047. Implemented in 17 high-focus states across the country, this program aims to improve the care and prospects of all sickle cell disease patients while reducing the prevalence of the disease. (ANI)

top_news.title: "Congress sides with those who exploit women": Bansuri Swaraj seeks action against Akoijam in JNU harassment case
top_news.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Bansuri Swaraj on Thursday accused Congress leadership of remaining silent over sexual harassment allegations against Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, saying her party's delegation had approached Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking action in the matter. The BJP women MPs' delegation met the Lok Sabha Speaker and submitted a memorandum seeking action against Akoijam, a Congress MP from Inner Manipur, following allegations of sexual harassment involving 11 female students at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). Addressing a press conference after the meeting, Bansuri Swaraj said, "It is highly unfortunate that the Congress party consistently sides with those who exploit women. When Bimal Akoijam--a sitting MP from the Congress party--sexually harassed 11 female students, JNU's internal committee found that the complaints filed by these students against him were truthful and substantiated by facts." She further said that Akoijam was dismissed from his position at JNU on October 9, 2026, following the internal committee's findings, and questioned the silence of senior Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Sonia Gandhi. "Yet, there is an absolutely deafening silence from Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Kharge ji, and Sonia Gandhi," Swaraj said. "Today, under the guidance and leadership of our Mahila Morcha National President and fellow MP, Rupkumari Choudhary, we met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Om Birla. We appealed to the President, Droupadi Murmu. Yesterday, a delegation met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW), Vijaya Rahatkar, and today, we submitted a memorandum to Om Birla. We had a very productive discussion," she added. BJP Mahila Morcha National President and MP Roop Kumari Chaudhary described the incident as "shameful" and said the party would continue to raise the issue until the students received justice and protection. Chaudhary said the party was concerned about the safety of the complainants, who continue to study at the university, and called on the Congress to suspend or expel Akoijam. "The incident that took place at JNU was truly shameful. JNU Professor Dr. Bimol Akoijam-who is also a Congress MP from Manipur-subjected 11 young women to mistreatment, sexual harassment, and abuse. Why haven't Congress leaders like Rahul Gandhi or Priyanka Gandhi come forward to stand up for these young women? Rahul Gandhi has not uttered a single word in support of these daughters. Instead, he has provided protection to Bimol Akoijam," she said. "The Bharatiya Janata Party's Mahila Morcha has taken to the streets in protest-to ensure that these daughters receive justice, their dignity is upheld, and they are provided with the protection they deserve. On the 12th October, we held a protest in Delhi. We also organized protests across the entire state on the 10th October, demanding that the Congress party take action against him. On 13th October, a delegation met with the President of India to ensure the protection of these young girls. On 14th October, we met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women, and today, a delegation of Members of Parliament met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. We argued that an individual facing such allegations has no right to sit in the House," she added. BJP Mahila Morcha National Vice President Daggubati Purandeswari also criticised Congress leadership, alleging that the party had failed to take action against Akoijam despite the university's internal inquiry. Purandeswari said the university's Vice-Chancellor had constituted an internal committee after complaints emerged, and the committee found Akoijam guilty of molesting 11 female students. She also referred to an interview in which Akoijam had reportedly spoken about the number of complaints against him, saying she was surprised that he had spoken about the complaints in that manner. Purandeswari praised the students for coming forward with their complaints, saying it required courage to speak out against a professor while studying at the same institution. Questioning Congress leaders' public positions on women's rights, she said, "On one hand we have Congress party leaders like Rahul Gandhi who says 'Smash the Patriarchy', and on the other hand we have Priyanka Gandhi ji who says 'Main ladki hoon, main lad sakti hoon' (I am a girl, I can fight). Today, we would like to question Priyanka Gandhi ji." She alleged that the Congress leadership's silence amounted to protecting Akoijam and called on the party to explain why it had not suspended or expelled him. Purandeswari also referred to allegations of misconduct against AAP MP Sanjay Singh during a recent protest involving BJP women workers, demanding an explanation from the opposition. A BJP women MPs' delegation, including Purandeswari, Swaraj and Chaudhary, met Speaker Birla and submitted a letter seeking action against Akoijam. The letter said the issue concerned "respect for women, safety of girl students, moral accountability in public life and conduct of political parties." According to the letter, "11 female students had filed sexual harassment complaints against Akoijam, who was a professor at JNU before becoming a Congress MP from Manipur. The university's Internal Committee conducted an inquiry and found the allegations against him to be substantiated, following which the administration issued an order on October 9, 2026, dismissing him from service with immediate effect." The delegation also attached copies of the FIR and other documents. On Wednesday, Chaudhary said NCW chairperson Vijaya K Rahatkar assured the delegation she would look into the matter. "We've been assured that she will definitely look into the matter given the situation," she said. "Once the investigation found him guilty, he was fired, but under Congress's protection, Congress leaders haven't said a single word about him yet," she alleged. JNU dismissed Akoijam with immediate effect on October 9 after its Internal Committee recommended major punishment following an inquiry under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act. Akoijam had earlier accused the administration of failing to provide him a copy of the inquiry report, needed to exercise his right to appeal, and alleged a violation of confidentiality under Section 16 of the POSH Act. Separately, Delhi Police registered an FIR on October 11 at Vasant Kunj North police station on a complaint by JNU's Chief Security Officer, under Sections 75, 75(1)(i), 75(1)(iv) and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The matter is under investigation. Earlier, a delegation of BJP women leaders, including Lok Sabha MPs Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Bansuri Swaraj and Malvika Devi, Rajya Sabha MPs S. Phangnon Konyak and Geeta Shakya, and senior leader Rekha Sharma, met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum seeking strict action. (ANI)

articles.title: "Committed to support India's mission to eliminate Sickle cell disease": Habib Bennaceur, SVP Novo Nordisk
articles.summary: Novo Nordisk, a Danish multinational pharmaceutical company, has expressed support for India's mission to eliminate sickle cell disease by 2047, highlighting the need for early diagnosis, public awareness, better healthcare infrastructure and improved access to treatment. Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a chronic single gene disorder causing a debilitating systemic syndrome characterized by chronic anemia, acute painful episodes, organ infarction and chronic organ damage and by a significant reduction in life expectancy. Habib Bennaceur, Senior Vice President of the Rare Disease Unit at Novo Nordisk, said India accounts for a significant share of the global sickle cell disease burden, with around 10 million people living with the condition worldwide. Explaining the impact of the disease, speaking to ANI, Bennaceur said it affects the shape of red blood cells and their ability to carry oxygen, potentially causing anaemia and serious complications. "Actually, sickle cell disease is an inherited disease that will affect the red blood cell shapes and will limit the transport of oxygen, which is the role of the red blood cell, to organs and to the organism, which will result in anaemia. It might also result as well in multiple organ damage, strokes, heart issues, kidney failures, and also sickle cell disease is also very well known for vaso-occlusive crises, deep severe pain that will force patients to go to hospital and be hospitalised for a long duration sometimes. So it's a very severe disease that has multiple complex complications in the organism," Bennaceur said. Explaining the company's interest in the disease, he said the unmet medical needs of patients and Novo Nordisk's experience in treating blood disorders, particularly haemophilia, prompted it to invest in sickle cell disease. "Novo is first guided by the unmet need and patient needs. So sickle cell disease has been left on the side of innovation for a very long time. It's a large population globally; there are 10 million people living with sickle cell disease over the world. And India is the second largest country in that aspect. And our long legacy in haemophilia, so with our portfolio there, it was a natural move to go and invest in making a difference in sickle cell disease with the ambition to defeat sickle cell disease," he said. Bennaceur added that the company was committed to supporting patients, medical professionals and the central and state governments in achieving the 2047 target. "India is the second-largest country in the world in terms of sickle cell disease prevalence, which means as a global pharma company, as Novo, we cannot decently say we are invested in sickle cell disease if we don't support and make a difference in India. But India is facing what many countries globally are facing in terms of the severity of the disease and the complications, but India is leading in many ways, actually and in the understanding of the fact that if you want to improve sickle cell disease, you need to work first on diagnosis. You need to work first on awareness, education, and infrastructure. And that's again one of the reasons of our visits here is one to learn about the critical sickle cell disease mission elimination for 2047, but also to commit to the Indian community to support all patients, the medical community and also the government, central and state government, in that mission," he said. He said the company was supporting projects focused on improving diagnosis and awareness, including the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) Hub and wellness hub. He cited the lack of diagnosis and treatment as a major challenge in parts of sub-Saharan Africa. "We already started the support by working on many projects, one of them being the SPOC Hub, but also the wellness hub, which is obviously first to improve the first medical contact, working on first diagnosis and awareness. There's a reason why, in sub-Saharan African countries, for example, 90% of kids born with sickle cell disease will die before the age of five is because they're not diagnosed and thus not even treated," he said. He added that Novo Nordisk was developing potential treatments, with its most advanced candidate having reached Phase 3 trials with positive results. The results were scheduled to be presented at the American Society of Rheumatology Congress in December. Vikrant Shrotriya, Corporate Vice President and Managing Director of Novo Nordisk India, said clinical trials had been completed and the company was working with regulatory authorities to make the treatment available in India as soon as possible. "The trials are finished. We are working very closely, obviously, with regulatory authorities and relevant authorities here to make it available as soon as possible," Shrotriya said. Shrotriya said India had an estimated 1.5 million to two million people living with sickle cell disease and that the company was conducting research on potential treatments in the country. "Coming to the blood disorder, we came with one of our products called Nova 7. Over a period of time, we have got many factors in this area of haemophilia. So it was very natural that we started working in the sickle cell area. So we have got a couple of molecules, and for those molecules we are so proud because India has got a dubious distinction of being second in the world with the highest population of sickle cell, 1.5 to 2 million people. Every sixth or seventh person in the world for sickle cell is actually in India," he added. Expressing hope that the forum would strengthen efforts towards the 2047 target, Shrotriya said,"So I am very, very happy that along with the Danish Embassy, Novo Nordisk, Niti Aayog, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, many of the stakeholders who are involved therein have come together to take a pledge that we would work together for sickle cell elimination, which was called by Prime Minister Modi by 2047. So, this is just the start of that advocacy of that movement, and I wish and hope that this becomes strengthened over a period of time." The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (NSCEM) was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on July 1, 2023, with the goal of eliminating Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) as a public health problem in India by 2047. Implemented in 17 high-focus states across the country, this program aims to improve the care and prospects of all sickle cell disease patients while reducing the prevalence of the disease. (ANI)

articles.title: "Congress sides with those who exploit women": Bansuri Swaraj seeks action against Akoijam in JNU harassment case
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Bansuri Swaraj on Thursday accused Congress leadership of remaining silent over sexual harassment allegations against Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, saying her party's delegation had approached Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking action in the matter. The BJP women MPs' delegation met the Lok Sabha Speaker and submitted a memorandum seeking action against Akoijam, a Congress MP from Inner Manipur, following allegations of sexual harassment involving 11 female students at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU). Addressing a press conference after the meeting, Bansuri Swaraj said, "It is highly unfortunate that the Congress party consistently sides with those who exploit women. When Bimal Akoijam--a sitting MP from the Congress party--sexually harassed 11 female students, JNU's internal committee found that the complaints filed by these students against him were truthful and substantiated by facts." She further said that Akoijam was dismissed from his position at JNU on October 9, 2026, following the internal committee's findings, and questioned the silence of senior Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Sonia Gandhi. "Yet, there is an absolutely deafening silence from Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Kharge ji, and Sonia Gandhi," Swaraj said. "Today, under the guidance and leadership of our Mahila Morcha National President and fellow MP, Rupkumari Choudhary, we met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Om Birla. We appealed to the President, Droupadi Murmu. Yesterday, a delegation met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW), Vijaya Rahatkar, and today, we submitted a memorandum to Om Birla. We had a very productive discussion," she added. BJP Mahila Morcha National President and MP Roop Kumari Chaudhary described the incident as "shameful" and said the party would continue to raise the issue until the students received justice and protection. Chaudhary said the party was concerned about the safety of the complainants, who continue to study at the university, and called on the Congress to suspend or expel Akoijam. "The incident that took place at JNU was truly shameful. JNU Professor Dr. Bimol Akoijam-who is also a Congress MP from Manipur-subjected 11 young women to mistreatment, sexual harassment, and abuse. Why haven't Congress leaders like Rahul Gandhi or Priyanka Gandhi come forward to stand up for these young women? Rahul Gandhi has not uttered a single word in support of these daughters. Instead, he has provided protection to Bimol Akoijam," she said. "The Bharatiya Janata Party's Mahila Morcha has taken to the streets in protest-to ensure that these daughters receive justice, their dignity is upheld, and they are provided with the protection they deserve. On the 12th October, we held a protest in Delhi. We also organized protests across the entire state on the 10th October, demanding that the Congress party take action against him. On 13th October, a delegation met with the President of India to ensure the protection of these young girls. On 14th October, we met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women, and today, a delegation of Members of Parliament met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. We argued that an individual facing such allegations has no right to sit in the House," she added. BJP Mahila Morcha National Vice President Daggubati Purandeswari also criticised Congress leadership, alleging that the party had failed to take action against Akoijam despite the university's internal inquiry. Purandeswari said the university's Vice-Chancellor had constituted an internal committee after complaints emerged, and the committee found Akoijam guilty of molesting 11 female students. She also referred to an interview in which Akoijam had reportedly spoken about the number of complaints against him, saying she was surprised that he had spoken about the complaints in that manner. Purandeswari praised the students for coming forward with their complaints, saying it required courage to speak out against a professor while studying at the same institution. Questioning Congress leaders' public positions on women's rights, she said, "On one hand we have Congress party leaders like Rahul Gandhi who says 'Smash the Patriarchy', and on the other hand we have Priyanka Gandhi ji who says 'Main ladki hoon, main lad sakti hoon' (I am a girl, I can fight). Today, we would like to question Priyanka Gandhi ji." She alleged that the Congress leadership's silence amounted to protecting Akoijam and called on the party to explain why it had not suspended or expelled him. Purandeswari also referred to allegations of misconduct against AAP MP Sanjay Singh during a recent protest involving BJP women workers, demanding an explanation from the opposition. A BJP women MPs' delegation, including Purandeswari, Swaraj and Chaudhary, met Speaker Birla and submitted a letter seeking action against Akoijam. The letter said the issue concerned "respect for women, safety of girl students, moral accountability in public life and conduct of political parties." According to the letter, "11 female students had filed sexual harassment complaints against Akoijam, who was a professor at JNU before becoming a Congress MP from Manipur. The university's Internal Committee conducted an inquiry and found the allegations against him to be substantiated, following which the administration issued an order on October 9, 2026, dismissing him from service with immediate effect." The delegation also attached copies of the FIR and other documents. On Wednesday, Chaudhary said NCW chairperson Vijaya K Rahatkar assured the delegation she would look into the matter. "We've been assured that she will definitely look into the matter given the situation," she said. "Once the investigation found him guilty, he was fired, but under Congress's protection, Congress leaders haven't said a single word about him yet," she alleged. JNU dismissed Akoijam with immediate effect on October 9 after its Internal Committee recommended major punishment following an inquiry under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act. Akoijam had earlier accused the administration of failing to provide him a copy of the inquiry report, needed to exercise his right to appeal, and alleged a violation of confidentiality under Section 16 of the POSH Act. Separately, Delhi Police registered an FIR on October 11 at Vasant Kunj North police station on a complaint by JNU's Chief Security Officer, under Sections 75, 75(1)(i), 75(1)(iv) and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The matter is under investigation. Earlier, a delegation of BJP women leaders, including Lok Sabha MPs Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Bansuri Swaraj and Malvika Devi, Rajya Sabha MPs S. Phangnon Konyak and Geeta Shakya, and senior leader Rekha Sharma, met President Droupadi Murmu and submitted a memorandum seeking strict action. (ANI)
